events.continuity_hook: Continues the Blue Ridge weekend from the packet-pickup and storm-timing question, aiming to settle the travel plan without overcorrecting close to departure.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm that the regional-airport plan still protects packet pickup and Friday check-in, verify the lodge amenity notes, and decide whether to leave the flight and rental car unchanged.
events.scenario_brief: The Blue Ridge trail organizer adds a late Friday packet-pickup window after weather concerns, and the regional airport rental counter confirms Kara and her partner's car will be held if their Tampa connection is mildly late. The larger-airport itinerary still arrives earlier on paper but now costs more and adds nearly two extra hours of driving before check-in. The lodge keeps the queen room, notes the mini-fridge request again, and says the hot tub opens after dinner; the remaining question is whether the small gain in arrival certainty is worth changing airports.

events.continuity_hook: Returns to Columbus after the main pieces were chosen, with only timing, commute, and arrival details left to settle.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the Monday arrival, Tuesday commute, Wednesday connection, and hotel details, then decide whether the current itinerary is safe enough to keep.
events.scenario_brief: With the Columbus coaching visit close enough for final emails, the hospital moves Tuesday morning arrival to a staff entrance by a different garage, and the airline trims Kara's Wednesday evening connection. The airport-area hotel confirms the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool, and fitness room, but still no listed hot tub; the first hospital commute still has to work for a 7:15 a.m. start. The open decision is whether the existing Wednesday return is still practical or whether to pay for the Thursday morning nonstop and one extra night.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new fall seminar episode after the Blue Ridge and Columbus logistics have mostly cleared.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, compare campus convenience against room reliability, and list what the host must confirm before Kara commits.
events.scenario_brief: A Raleigh pediatric therapy network asks Kara to teach a late-September gait seminar with Friday afternoon setup, a full Saturday course, and a Sunday lab whose end time is not yet fixed. She can leave Tampa only after a Thursday noon teaching block, and the host site is near a university hospital where traffic is predictable only outside shift-change hours. Flight options are workable but not abundant, and hotels divide between a campus-adjacent property with uneven recent feedback and better-rated chain options 12 to 18 minutes away with clearer room basics.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Raleigh seminar after the lab end time and hotel facts make the main trade-offs bookable.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the hotel, select a Sunday return that leaves enough teardown and airport cushion, and request a window seat if seat selection is available.
events.scenario_brief: The Raleigh host confirms the Sunday lab will end by 1:00 p.m. and can receive Kara's demo items before Friday setup. The closest campus hotel is convenient but still shows weaker guest ratings and mostly double-bed listings; a better-rated suite hotel 15 minutes away has a queen room with coffee maker and mini-fridge plus pool and fitness access, though no hot tub. Sunday returns now cluster around 4:40 p.m. and 6:35 p.m., leaving a choice between a tighter airport transfer and a later Tampa arrival.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a larger conference-planning episode while the fall seminar calendar is taking shape.
events.interaction_goal: Compare flights, the connected room block, the offsite suite option, and Sunday return timing before the best rooms fill.
events.scenario_brief: Registration opens for an October pediatric rehab conference in San Antonio with a Thursday afternoon pre-course, Friday and Saturday sessions, and a Sunday closing panel ending around noon. Kara can leave Tampa after a Wednesday morning class but needs enough recovery time before teaching again Monday. The connected conference hotel is in the official block with a solid rating but unclear in-room fridge availability, while a nearby suite hotel has stronger room details and more recovery amenities but requires a short ride or walk to the convention center.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the San Antonio conference plan after hotel availability and amenity details narrow the choice.
events.interaction_goal: Pick the conference hotel strategy, select a Sunday return that does not rush the closing panel, and book the main pieces with a window seat if available.
events.scenario_brief: The San Antonio room block begins filling faster than expected, and the connected hotel confirms a coffee maker and queen room but only limited mini-fridges by request; its pool will also be unavailable during one maintenance day. The offsite suite still has a cancellable queen room with coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness room, but its shuttle starts too late for the Thursday pre-course. Return flights after the Sunday panel include a tight early-afternoon departure and a more comfortable late-afternoon option.
